name: Beta Comae Berenices
description: A naked-eye star 9.1 parsecs away, 1.1 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 114710: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.127 +/- 0.011 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.106 +/- 0.011

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 114710: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.045 +/- 0.013

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 114710: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5936 +/- 33

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 114710: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 109.53 +/- 0.17 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 9 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 1.1 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1.127 milliarcseconds, which gives 1.106 solar radii and 5,936 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 114710: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
